source_text: Dicunt sanctos in Vetere Testamento non caruisse peccatis, id est, nec per emendationem a criminibus fuisse liberos, sed in reatu a morte fuisse deprehensos.
pass_a_gloss: They say that the saints in the Old Testament were not without sins: that is, they were not free from crimes even through correction, but were caught in guilt by death.

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS liber=free; Blaise unde liberum est abstinere

pass_b_english: They say that the saints of the Old Testament were not free from sins: that is, even by correcting their lives they were not freed from wrongdoing, but death overtook them while they were still guilty.

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.
Freedom to abstain is required for will and sin.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (Letter to Rome, words preserved in Augustine, Contra duas epistolas Pelagianorum 1); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
